Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)
```

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
```

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)
```

### Create Layered Material for Wall

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Creates a layered material set with multiple layers and assigns it to an IfcWallType. This is useful for representing complex wall constructions. It involves creating individual materials, a material layer set, adding layers with thicknesses, and finally assigning the set to a wall type.

```python
import ifcopenshell.api.material

# Create materials
concrete = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="Concrete")
insulation = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="Insulation")

# Create material layer set
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(
    model,
    name="200mm Insulated Wall",
    set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet"
)

# Add layers (from outside to inside)
layer1 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(
    model,
    layer_set=material_set,
    material=concrete
)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(
    model,
    layer=layer1,
    attributes={"LayerThickness": 0.10, "Description": "Exterior concrete"}
)

layer2 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(
    model,
    layer_set=material_set,
    material=insulation
)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(
    model,
    layer=layer2,
    attributes={"LayerThickness": 0.08, "Description": "Thermal insulation"}
)

layer3 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(
    model,
    layer_set=material_set,

import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from typing import List

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:
                    thickness = qset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    
    return violating_guids

# Test on all available models
models_to_test = [
    '/home/sffc348/Repos/cobbie/acc/bim_models/duplex/arc.ifc',

    '/home/sffc348/Repos/cobbie/acc/bim_models/dental_clinic/arc.ifc'
]

for model_path in models_to_test:

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)

# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")
```

    """
    # Define parameters

    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements

    if not slabs:

    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType

            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:

            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set

            skipped_count += 1
            continue

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
```

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element

    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:
                    thickness = qset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    
    return violating_guids

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
```

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)
```

    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING',
    and excludes finish floor materials (slabs with 'Finish Floor' in name).
    
    Args:

        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    processed_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:

                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    processed_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get all psets (both properties and quantities)
            # Thickness can be in properties like PSet_Revit_Dimensions
            all_psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab)
            
            # Look for thickness in any pset (properties or quantities)
            thickness = None
            for pset_name, pset in all_psets.items():
                if 'Thickness' in pset:
                    thickness = pset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
            processed_count += 1
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    print(f"Processed {processed_count} slabs, found {len(violating_guids)} violations")
    
    return violating_guids

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")
```

    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:
                    thickness = qset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    
    return violating_guids

    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING',
    and excludes finish floor materials (slabs with 'Finish Floor' in name).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    processed_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Exclude finish floor materials (finish floors typically have small thickness
            # and are not structural slabs subject to the 0.30m minimum)
            slab_name = getattr(slab, 'Name', '')
            if 'Finish Floor' in slab_name:
                continue
            
            # Get all psets (both properties and quantities)
            # Thickness can be in properties like PSet_Revit_Dimensions
            all_psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab)
            
            # Look for thickness in any pset (properties or quantities)
            thickness = None
            for pset_name, pset in all_psets.items():
                if 'Thickness' in pset:
                    thickness = pset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
            processed_count += 1
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    print(f"Processed {processed_count} slabs, found {len(violating_guids)} violations")
    
    return violating_guids

import ifcopenshell.util.placement

    else:

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({

        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING',
    and excludes finish floor materials (slabs with 'Finish Floor' in name).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:

    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    processed_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
```

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)
```

### Create Layered Material for Wall

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Creates a layered material set with multiple layers and assigns it to an IfcWallType. This is useful for representing complex wall constructions. It involves creating individual materials, a material layer set, adding layers with thicknesses, and finally assigning the set to a wall type.

```python
import ifcopenshell.api.material

# Create materials
concrete = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="Concrete")
insulation = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="Insulation")
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="Gypsum")

# Create material layer set
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(
    model,
    name="200mm Insulated Wall",
    set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet"
)

# Add layers (from outside to inside)
layer1 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(
    model,
    layer_set=material_set,
    material=concrete

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
```

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model

    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:
                    thickness = qset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    
    return violating_guids

import ifcopenshell

import ifcopenshell.util.placement

    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

### Manage Material Layer Sets for Wall Types in IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates the process of creating a wall type with a material layer set using IfcOpenShell. This includes defining materials, layers with thicknesses, assigning the material set to the type, and then creating a wall instance with compatible geometry.

```python
# Let's imagine a wall type called WAL01 using a material layer set.
wall_type = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWallType", name="WAL01")

# First, let's create a material set. This will later be assigned to our wall type element.
material_set = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material_set(model,
    name="GYP-ST-GYP", set_type="IfcMaterialLayerSet")

# Let's create a few materials.
gypsum = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="PB01", category="gypsum")
steel = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_material(model, name="ST01", category="steel")

# Create 3 layers for a steel studded plasterboard wall.
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=steel)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 92})
layer = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_layer(model, layer_set=material_set, material=gypsum)
ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_layer(model, layer=layer, attributes={"LayerThickness": 13})

# Great! Let's assign our material set to our wall type.
ifcopenshell.api.material.assign_material(model, products=[wall_type], material=material_set)

# Now, let's create a wall at the origin.
wall = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcWall")
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=wall)

# The wall is a WAL01 wall type. The material layer set is inherited.
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[wall], relating_type=wall_type)

# It's now our responsibility to create a compatible representation.
# Notice how our thickness of 0.118 must equal .013 + .092 + .013 from our type
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = ifcopenshell.api.geometry.add_wall_representation(model,
    context=body, length=5, height=3, thickness=0.118)

# Assign our new body geometry back to our wall
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=wall, representation=representation)

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")
```

### Calculate Total Quantities per Level using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Calculates and aggregates quantities (like wall count and total volume) for each level in an IFC model. It iterates through walls, determines their level, extracts volume data from property sets, and prints a summary.

```python
import ifcopenshell.util.element
from collections import defaultdict

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
quantities_by_level = defaultdict(lambda: {"wall_count": 0, "total_volume": 0.0})

for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)
    level = container.Name if container else "Unassigned"

    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)
    volume = psets.get('Qto_WallBaseQuantities', {}).get('GrossVolume', 0.0)

    quantities_by_level[level]["wall_count"] += 1
    quantities_by_level[level]["total_volume"] += volume

for level, data in quantities_by_level.items():
    print(f"{level}: {data['wall_count']} walls, {data['total_volume']:.2f} m³")

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Get quantities (thickness is usually in Qto_SlabBaseQuantities)
            qtos = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab, qtos_only=True)
            
            # Look for thickness in any quantity set
            thickness = None
            for qset_name, qset in qtos.items():
                if 'Thickness' in qset:
                    thickness = qset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules
            if thickness < MIN_THICKNESS or thickness > MAX_THICKNESS:
                violating_guids.append(slab.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} elements due to missing data or errors")
    
    return violating_guids

import ifcopenshell

def check_slab_thickness(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: BIM Validation: Slab Thickness slab_thickness
    
    Checks that slab thickness is not too small or too large. 
    Minimum thickness: 0.30 m, Maximum thickness: 1.0 m.
    
    Excludes slabs with PredefinedType 'FIXED_FURNISHING' or 'SUSPENDED_CEILING',
    and excludes finish floor materials (slabs with 'Finish Floor' in name).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of all slab elements that violate the thickness rule.
        
    Example:
        >>> violating_guids = check_slab_thickness('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f'Found {len(violating_guids)} violations')
    """
    # Define parameters
    MIN_THICKNESS = 0.30  # meters
    MAX_THICKNESS = 1.0   # meters
    EXCLUDED_TYPES = {'FIXED_FURNISHING', 'SUSPENDED_CEILING'}
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    processed_count = 0
    
    # Get all IfcSlab elements
    slabs = model.by_type('IfcSlab')
    
    if not slabs:
        return []
    
    for slab in slabs:
        try:
            # Check if slab should be excluded based on PredefinedType
            predefined_type = getattr(slab, 'PredefinedType', None)
            if predefined_type in EXCLUDED_TYPES:
                continue
            
            # Exclude finish floor materials (finish floors typically have small thickness
            # and are not structural slabs subject to the 0.30m minimum)
            slab_name = getattr(slab, 'Name', '')
            if 'Finish Floor' in slab_name:
                continue
            
            # Get all psets (both properties and quantities)
            # Thickness can be in properties like PSet_Revit_Dimensions
            all_psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(slab)
            
            # Look for thickness in any pset (properties or quantities)
            thickness = None
            for pset_name, pset in all_psets.items():
                if 'Thickness' in pset:
                    thickness = pset['Thickness']
                    break
            
            if thickness is None:

                continue
            
            # Check if thickness violates rules

### Extract Wall Data to Structured Format (CSV) using IFCopenShell

Source: https://context7.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/llms.txt

Extracts detailed data from IfcWall elements, including properties, placement, type, and assigned quantities, into a structured format and saves it as a CSV file using Pandas. It utilizes utility functions for element and placement manipulation.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.element
import ifcopenshell.util.placement
import pandas as pd

# Assuming 'model' is an opened IFC model
# model = ifcopenshell.open("building.ifc")

wall_data = []
for wall in model.by_type("IfcWall"):
    # Get properties
    psets = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(wall)

    # Get position
    if wall.ObjectPlacement:
        matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
        position = matrix[:,3][:3]
    else:
        position = [0, 0, 0]

    # Get container
    container = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_container(wall)

    # Get type
    wall_type = ifcopenshell.util.element.get_type(wall)

    wall_data.append({
        'GlobalId': wall.GlobalId,
        'Name': wall.Name,
        'Type': wall_type.Name if wall_type else None,
        'Level': container.Name if container else None,
        'X': float(position[0]),
        'Y': float(position[1]),
        'Z': float(position[2]),
        'FireRating': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('FireRating'),
        'IsExternal': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('IsExternal'),
        'LoadBearing': psets.get('Pset_WallCommon', {}).get('LoadBearing'),
    })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(wall_data)
df.to_csv("walls_export.csv", index=False)
print(df)
